newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-AWAY WINS PILE PRESSURE ON ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AWAY WINS PILE PRESSURE ON ENGLAND.

text.p: England could face a battle to retain their Five Nations title after Wales and France set a cracking pace in this season's championship with significant victories on Saturday.
For the first time for five years, both opening matches produced away wins and offered further evidence to support the theory this is one of the most open tournaments for years.

Neither the 34-19 Welsh win in Scotland nor the French side's 32-15 success in Dublin were world-beating performances but are sure to do wonders for each side's confidence at a time of creeping self-doubt at Twickenham.
England coach Jack Rowell is set to reveal his plans on Monday for his side's opening game against Scotland on February 1 but his season will probably get tougher the longer it lasts.
The English face the French at home sandwiched between awkward visits to Dublin and Cardiff and must make some tricky decisions about tactics and selection.

They could do worse than take a leaf out of the Welsh book. Three tries in the space of five minutes gave a misleading look to the victory margin, but the Welsh backs relished the chance to run and all did their Lions prospects a power of good.

Scott Quinnell also had a huge game at number eight, scoring the first of his side's four tries. Captain Jonathan Humphreys believes the extra muscle provided by the returned rugby league contingent has been a crucial factor.

"Some of the hits Scott Gibbs made were phenomenal," he said. "All the rugby league boys bring a great deal of confidence to the side and a very mature attitude which rubs off on the rest of the players."
Scotland took due note and are likely to restore their own ex-rugby league man Alan Tait to the centre against England to stiffen their defence.

Captain Rob Wainwright blamed lapses of concentration for the three crucial tries but Scottish director of rugby Jim Telfer felt the two sides had been more evenly matched than the scoreline indicated.

One disappointed former Scottish international dismissed the Welsh as "not a great side" but a win against Ireland in Cardiff in a fortnight will present them with an outstanding chance of winning their first Triple Crown for nine years.

The Irish have kept the Welsh at bay at the the Arms Park since 1983 but may have to do without hooker and captain Keith Wood for the rest of the championship after he dislocated a shoulder against France.

His side competed well for the first hour at Lansdowne Road before running short of steam as Brive winger David Venditti joined the rare club of players to score a hat-trick of tries in a Five Nations game.
The French sit out the next round of matches but welcome Wales to Parc des Princes on February 15 in an encounter which, in title terms, could now prove the most decisive 80 minutes of all.
